doneAndVerified.design: Refactored the one-directional, numeric-only comparison into an exported pure function `compareTables(jurisdictionKey, vendored, corpus)` returning typed mismatches, now checking BOTH directions (set equality on district names, not one-way containment) AND provenance monotonicity (verification_state must not weaken). The monotonicity rank is deliberately NOT the naive one (human-verified highest): rank is asserted=0 < human-verified=1 < primary-source-verified=2, with an inline comment explaining why -- human-verified has now shipped fabricated twice in this corpus (Round Rock's original correction, and this Kyle regression), so it is a claim this corpus has learned to distrust, while primary-source-verified is the earned ceiling for a jurisdiction confirmed to have zero atoms. Under this ranking, Kyle's actual regression (primary-source-verified -> human-verified) IS a rank decrease, i.e. correctly caught.
